article_content: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb army commander, went on trial for crimes against humanity. He's accused of being directly involved in the Srebrenica massacre, where approximately 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys were killed. A judge at The Hague tribunal described the events as 'truly scenes from hell written on the darkest pages of human history.' Mladic was born in 1942 in Kalinovik, Bosnia-Herzegovina. He graduated from a military academy in 1965 and joined the Communist Party in Yugoslavia. Mladic's forces besieged Sarajevo, killing over 10,000 people, mostly civilians. The three-year war resulted in over 100,000 deaths, making it one of the bloodiest conflicts in Europe since World War II.

article_content: China is revamping its lending approach to developing nations, shifting from large bilateral agreements to collaborative lending that mitigates financial risk, according to a report by AidData at William and Mary. This change results in a moderate decrease in spending, yet China still surpasses G7 countries in aid and loans. In 2021, China provided '$79 billion' in aid and loans to low- and middle-income nations, exceeding the '$61 billion' provided by the US. China's new strategy involves syndicated loans with Western commercial banks and multilateral institutions, enhancing its efficiency as a lender.

article_content: A mine exploded on Monday on a road in southern Somalia, killing four people -- three members of the medical humanitarian group 'Medecins Sans Frontieres' (MSF) and a journalist. The incident occurred along a road in Kismayo, a city in southern Somalia. The MSF workers killed were Victor Okumu, 51, a Kenyan doctor; Damien Lehalle, 27, a French logistician; and a Somali driver named Billan. Journalist Hassan Kafi Hared, 36, who worked for the government-run Somali National News Agency and the Somali website 'gedonet.com', was also killed. The remote-controlled mine erupted as he was walking to a news conference in 'Siyad Village' in Kismayo.

Incident se dogodio na putu u Kismayu. Ubijeni pripadnici MSF-a bili su Victor Okumu, 51-godišnji kenijski doktor; Damien Lehalle, 27-godišnji francuski logističar; i somalijski vozač po imenu Billan. Također, ubijen je novinar Hassan Kafi Hared, 36 godina, koji je radio za Somalijsku nacionalnu novinsku agenciju i somalijski web sajt 'gedonet.com'. Daljinski aktivirana mina je eksplodirala dok je on išao na konferenciju za novinare u selu 'Siyad' u Kismayu.

article_content: The daily lives of medieval townsfolk have been brought to light by an extraordinary collection of graffiti discovered in Norwich Cathedral. Messages were scratched into the walls of this historic building over hundreds of years, but few have attempted to decipher them. Archaeologists from the Norfolk Medieval Graffiti Survey have initiated a major project to interpret these messages, uncovering a mix of musical compositions, pious exhortations, and even supernatural curses. 'The walls are covered in everything you can think of,' said project director Matthew Champion. 'Medieval ships, names, animals, windmills, figures, and prayers - just about everything important to Norwich's citizens during the Middle Ages.' The graffiti includes a ship being swallowed by a whale, possibly symbolizing Jonah's whale, and musical notes that the cathedral's organist hopes to play.

Arheolozi iz 'Norfolk Medieval Graffiti Survey' su pokrenuli veliki projekat kako bi interpretirali ove poruke, otkrivajući mješavinu muzičkih kompozicija, pobožnih zapisa i natprirodnih kletvi. 'Zidovi su prekriveni svim što možete zamisliti,' rekao je direktor projekta Matthew Champion.

article_content: Massachusetts health officials have reported the state's first case of Eastern Equine Encephalitis (EEE) this year, a potentially deadly virus transmitted by mosquito bites. The individual infected with EEE was identified in Plymouth County with a positive lab test on July 15th. EEE is known to cause severe symptoms including brain inflammation and can be fatal in about a third of cases. The virus is primarily carried by birds and then transmitted to humans through mosquitoes. Symptoms of EEE include fever, severe joint pain, swelling, rashes, and prolonged arthritis-like sensations. It's crucial to note that EEE cannot be transmitted directly from human to human. Meanwhile, Florida has reported its first two cases of chikungunya, another mosquito-borne disease. The cases in Florida were identified in Miami-Dade and Palm Beach counties, with symptoms appearing in late June and early July. Chikungunya causes symptoms such as fever, severe joint pain, and swelling. Health officials are taking preventive measures including increased spraying in mosquito-prone areas and advising property owners to eliminate standing water and seal windows.

article_content: It is something all human beings do, regardless of where they live, how they worship, or what they believe: They sleep. Except that for a growing number of Americans, sleep has become a luxury they can't afford. Pat Foucht, 67, lives in upstate New York. Eight years ago, she developed breast cancer and underwent extensive medical treatments. Ever since, her life has not been the same. 'I'm just wide awake all night long,' she says. 'And sometimes now, I'll wake up and can't get back to sleep. But it's mainly falling asleep.' Foucht is one of an estimated 100 million Americans who regularly suffer from insomnia, either because they are taking medication, or experiencing pain, or not eating right. Or -- according to Russell Rosenberg, who directs the Sleep Medicine Institute in Atlanta, Georgia -- sometimes it is simply because they are living in the 'always-on' modern world. 'It's a 24/7 society now,' Dr. Rosenberg notes. 'You have Internet 24/7, television, radio. Everything can keep you distracted from the time you need to sleep. Plus, people are working harder, working more jobs, trying to squeeze in more family-time, more leisure-time, and so forth, and so there's only so much time to do the things we want to do in one particular day.' According to an annual poll conducted by the National Sleep Foundation, in 2005, 90 percent of Americans experienced sleeping problems ranging from minor and transient to severe and chronic. That's up from 62 percent in 1999, when the NSF first conducted its poll. The number of Americans turning to prescription sleep aids for help has gone up dramatically: nearly 100 percent over the past five years. American pharmacists filled about 60 million sleeping pill prescriptions last year, and most were for either Ambien or Lunesta, two recent additions to the sleep aid market. These drugs aren't believed to be habit-forming, but they have serious side-effects that earlier sleep aids didn't have. For that reason, Russell Rosenberg says they can be a risky option for certain patients. 'For something we consider very short-term or transient,' he says, 'like the death of a loved one, most physicians will realize this person just needs a few tablets to get them through the stress.' At the same time, there's evidence that these new sleeping pills may have significant side-effects. Some people who have taken them reported short-term amnesia. Pat Foucht says she feels side-effects the morning after taking a prescription sleep medication. 'I take something now when I have this problem, and I've found that I'm groggy in the morning. And I may be a little more depressed.' For that reason, sleep experts prefer treating patients with 'cognitive behavioral therapy,' or CBT. It's a form of psychotherapy that changes how a patient thinks, feels, and acts about sleep. It doesn't yield immediate results, though, and in many parts of the country, it's unavailable. There are only about 50 clinicians worldwide with extensive CBT training in sleep. That's part of why prescription drugs have become so popular. But the biggest reason, says Gregg Jacobs, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, is marketing. 'You'll see their ads every night on TV now. They're the most frequent drug ads on TV,' he notes. 'As a result, people around the US -- and soon worldwide -- are given the message that a sleeping pill can cure insomnia. And when people hear that, they rush out to buy this pill.' Last year, drug companies spent over $600 million on ads for prescription sleep aids, more than four times what they spent in 2004. But Gregg Jacobs has unveiled his own weapon against insomnia: an interactive website, cbtforinsomnia.com. Patients sign on and have regular telephone and Internet consultations with a trained clinician who could be two or 2,000 kilometers away. Results from a study funded by the National Institutes of Health indicate CBT may be more effective than prescription medication or face-to-face therapy in treating insomnia.

Iz tog razloga, Russell Rosenberg kaže da oni mogu biti rizična opcija za određene pacijente. 'Za nešto što smatramo vrlo kratkoročnim ili prolaznim,' kaže on, 'poput smrti voljene osobe, većina liječnika će shvatiti da ta osoba treba samo nekoliko tableta da prebrodi stres.' U isto vrijeme, postoje dokazi da ovi novi lijekovi za spavanje mogu imati značajne nuspojave. Neki ljudi koji su ih uzimali prijavili su kratkoročni gubitak pamćenja. Pat Foucht kaže da osjeća nuspojave ujutro nakon uzimanja lijeka za spavanje. 'Uzimam nešto sada kada imam ovaj problem, i ustanovila sam da sam pospana ujutro. I možda sam malo depresivnija.' Iz tog razloga, stručnjaci za san preferiraju liječenje pacijenata sa 'kognitivno-bihejvioralnom terapijom,' ili CBT. To je oblik psihoterapije koji mijenja način na koji pacijent razmišlja, osjeća i djeluje u vezi sa spavanjem. Ono ne daje trenutne rezultate, i u mnogim dijelovima zemlje, nije dostupno. Postoji samo oko 50 kliničara širom svijeta sa opsežnom CBT obukom u oblasti sna. To je dio razloga zašto su lijekovi na recept postali toliko popularni. Ali najveći razlog, kaže Gregg Jacobs, docent psihijatrije na Harvard Medical School, je marketing. 'Vidjet ćete njihove reklame svake večeri na TV-u sada. To su najčešće reklame za lijekove na TV-u,' napominje on. 'Kao rezultat toga, ljudima širom SAD-a -- i uskoro širom svijeta -- se daje poruka da tableta za spavanje može izliječiti nesanicu. I kada ljudi to čuju, oni požure da kupe ovu tabletu.' Prošle godine, farmaceutske kompanije su potrošile pre- više od $600 miliona na reklame za lijekove za spavanje na recept, više od četiri puta više nego što su potrošile u 2004. godini. Ali Gregg Jacobs je predstavio svoje vlastito oružje protiv nesanice: interaktivnu web stranicu, cbtforinsomnia.com. Pacijenti se registruju i imaju redovne telefonske i Internet konsultacije sa obučenim kliničarom koji može biti dva ili 2.000 kilometara udaljen. Rezultati studije koju je finansirao Nacionalni institut za zdravlje ukazuju da CBT može biti efikasniji od lijekova na recept ili terapije licem u lice u liječenju nesanice.

article_content: AL-HASAKAH, SYRIA - At least '40' civilians were killed Tuesday in a surprise Islamic State attack outside a refugee camp on the Syrian side of the border with Iraq, according to 'eyewitnesses and Kurdish officials'. The predawn assault occurred in the Rajm al-Salibeh region, a front-line zone between IS and U.S.-backed forces where Syrian and Iraqi refugees fleeing IS territory gather before entering the Kurdish-controlled region in northern Syria. Dozens of armed IS militants on motorcycles and in cars approached '500' refugee families from Iraq's Mosul and Syria's Deir Ezzor who were waiting overnight in a makeshift stopover on their way to al-Houl refugee camp. This frame grab from video provided by the Hawar News Agency shows people wounded in the attack receiving treatment at a clinic in al-Hasakah province, Syria, May 2, 2017. 'At least seven suicide attackers blew themselves up,' said Rami Abdel, a spokesman for the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. Fouad Omar, a Kurdish official in Qamishili, told VOA that IS fighters stabbed refugees and opened gunfire. 'We saw some cars coming to us from a distance and thought they were people fleeing from IS. But as soon as we went out of the tents, it became clear they were IS fighters,' a female survivor from Deir Ezzor told VOA. While being treated at a hospital in Hasakah for her wounds, the woman said refugees were deliberately targeted by IS for seeking safety among U.S.-backed Syrian Democratic Forces. 'They told us, 'You are infidels. You are with infidels. They started going to each tent and blindly open fire at people. It became the end of the world after half an hour. They killed everyone and left,' she said. The attack sparked heavy confrontation between IS and the U.S-backed SDF, whose fighters are gearing up for an assault on Raqqa. 'Our colleagues stood against the IS attack and were able to kill '20' fighters,' said Nisreen Abdullah, spokesperson of the Women Protection Units, a Kurdish female brigade. Abdullah said IS likely took advantage of rising tensions between the U.S.-backed forces and Turkey on the border to unleash the attacks. 'The number of our guards on the Iraqi-Syrian border is smaller now as we have dispatched more troops to guard our border with Turkey,' she said. Kurdish officials say refugees have been streaming into camps for months without incident. 'We welcomed more than '750,000' refugees from this area,' said Kurdish official Omar. Separately, near Damascus, the International Committee of the Red Cross said an aid convoy reached the besieged town of Douma for the first time since October. An ICRC tweet said the convoy entered the town under the cover of darkness, with '75' trucks carrying emergency supplies for '50,000' people. Rebel-held Douma has been under government siege for nearly four years. VOA's Rikar Hussein and Ahed Al Hendi contributed to this report from Washington.

article_content: The 'European Union' has imposed a 'total' arms embargo on 'the West African nation' of Guinea. The decision was made in response to the 'brutal suppression' of anti-government protesters last month by Guinea's 'ruthless' security forces. The European Union has banned the transfer of arms from the European Union to Guinea and also says it will restrict travel and freeze the assets of members of junta leader Captain Moussa Dadis Camara's government. Captain Camara seized power in a 'violent' military coup last December. A statement from EU ministers said they had decided to punish Guinea's rulers because, in their words, of the 'gross violations of human rights, including many deaths, injuries and rapes' that took place last month. According to the United Nations, security forces in Guinea opened fire on protesters killing more than '200' people on September 28 in the capital, Conakry. The government says more than 50 people were killed. Mike Lewis, of the British watchdog Amnesty International, says Europe-based companies supplied some of the military equipment used in last month's 'atrocity'. He says security forces used anti-riot grenades that had come from France and drove armored vehicles supplied by a South African company owned by a major British defense manufacturer. 'Some of those are European and so the EU embargo does have real intent and is likely to have real bite, but it is true to say that international measures beyond the EU will be necessary to stop arms transfers that are likely to be used in recurrent violations,' said Lewis. Lewis says the Economic Community of West African States, also known as ECOWAS, has led the way in blocking arms to Guinea. 'ECOWAS already has a number of regional agreements in place which regulates and controls arms transfers into and within the ECOWAS region and so the leadership that they have shown in suspending arms transfers to Guinea from within the region is vital,' he said. Lewis says this arms embargo is crucial, but should have come sooner. 'The events we saw in Guinea last month were not an isolated incident, they were part of a decade of violent repression by Guinea security forces,' he said. The U.N. General Assembly is meeting this week in New York to discuss an Arms Trade Treaty that would regulate the import and export of arms. Lewis says this type of preventative measure is needed. 'States will decide whether to start negotiations for an international arms trade treaty, which will prevent transfers of arms likely to be used in serious violations of human rights well before the kind of major attacks and massacres of the kind we have seen in Guinea,' he said. A resolution on Guinea sponsored by seven nations, including major arms-exporter Britain, has been presented to the U.N. General Assembly. The International Criminal Court has also launched a preliminary investigation into possible crimes against humanity during the violence.

article_content: By Associated Press. The recession and slow recovery have widened the gap between the wealthiest Americans and others, according to a new study. The richest 5% of Americans had 24 times the wealth of the median household in 2013, up from 16.5 times in 2007. Substantial stock market gains enabled richer Americans to regain wealth, while middle-class Americans remain behind due to their wealth being mainly derived from home equity. Home prices have only partially recovered from the housing bust. The home ownership rate fell to 64.8% in the first quarter of this year from 69.2% in 2004. The University of Michigan study found that households at all levels lost wealth during the recession. The study suggests that one reason consumer spending growth has been weaker since the recession is that when people feel wealthier, they're more likely to spend. The losses weren't evenly distributed; the top 5% saw a 16% drop in net worth from 2007 to last year, while the median household's net worth fell 43%. The study paints a bleaker picture of U.S. household wealth than official Federal Reserve figures.

Značajan rast na tržištu dionica omogućio je bogatijim Amerikancima da povrate bogatstvo, dok srednja klasa ostaje iza jer njihovo bogatstvo uglavnom potiče od vlasništva nad kućama. Cijene kuća su se samo djelimično oporavile od stambenog sloma. Stopa vlasništva kuća pala je na 64,8% u prvom kvartalu ove godine sa 69,2% u 2004. Studija Univerziteta u Michiganu pokazala je da su domaćinstva na svim nivoima izgubila bogatstvo tokom recesije. Studija sugerira da je jedan od razloga slabijeg rasta potrošnje taj što ljudi troše više kada se osjećaju bogatijima. article_content: An employee of 'Dixie River Freight Inc.', a trucking company based in 'Nampa, Idaho', abandoned a trailer containing '35,000 pounds' of frozen chicken at a western 'Montana' truck stop after the company refused to pay a ransom for the poultry, 'Missoula County' officials said. The '53-foot' trailer, dripping with the juices of rotting chicken, was discovered on 'Tuesday' near the 'Flying J Truck Stop' west of 'Missoula', the 'Missoulian' reported. Truck stop manager 'Crystal Friede' said the trailer had been there since at least 'Saturday'. It contained '35,000 pounds' of chicken worth '$80,000', officials said. The trucker texted 'Dixie River Freight Inc.' saying he'd return the chicken in exchange for a ransom, sheriff's spokeswoman 'Paige Pavalone' said on 'Wednesday'. The company refused his offer and reported the truck missing. A woman who answered the phone at 'Dixie River' declined to comment to 'The Associated Press'. 'Paige Pavalone' said the sheriff's office didn't know if the truck driver had been located. Officials with the county health department were at the truck stop on 'Wednesday' trying to figure out the best way to dispose of the load as temperatures in 'Missoula' topped '90 degrees'. 'It would be ideal to only have to deal with it once,' said 'Shannon Therriault', environmental health supervisor with the 'Missoula County Health Department'. 'We don't want rotting chicken dripping from here to who knows where. If it's leaking a little now, moving it could cause more leakage.' 'Republic Services' has an expert on staff to deal with rotten poultry, 'Therriault' said.

article_content: A woman, Amina Noor, 39, from Harrow, north-west London, has appeared at the Old Bailey accused of assisting in the female genital mutilation (FGM) of a three-year-old British girl in Kenya in 2006. However, a medical examination in 2019 found that the girl's clitoris had been completely removed. Ms Noor initially described accompanying another woman to a 'clinic' where the girl underwent the procedure, claiming she did not enter because she was 'scared and worried'. The girl was reportedly quiet afterwards, cried throughout the night, and complained of pain. Ms Noor later stated she had considered not going through with the FGM but decided to proceed. She referred to the act as 'Sunnah', a cultural tradition. The prosecution argued that Ms Noor 'encouraged and assisted' in the offence, questioning her claim that she expected only a minor procedure. The trial is ongoing.
